entries.clue: Supplies hose to cover end of street (6)

entries.clue: Cast actors in charge of teaching method (8)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast actors' reads as theatre casting; 'Cast' is the instruction to rearrange ACTORS.
annotation.definitionFit: The Socratic method teaches by asking a pupil a chain of questions, as Socrates did.

entries.clue: Fatefully, oxygen present in O- likely discharged (9)

indicators.note: the O for oxygen sits inside the word MINUS

annotation.walkthrough: The symbol 'O-' has to be spoken as 'O minus'; the oxygen then goes inside MINUS, giving O MIN(O)US before LY.

entries.clue: Philosophical German soldier supporting King (4)

entries.clue: Vintage Popeye in film recording that needs to be refined (5,3)

annotation.walkthrough: Popeye is not the sailor but Gene Hackman's detective 'Popeye' Doyle in The French Connection; 'cru Doyle' said quickly gives the answer.

entries.clue: Fierce diatribe about current measure (7)

entries.clue: Husband opening food store in megacity (5)

annotation.definitionFit: Delhi, with its tens of millions of inhabitants, is one of the world's megacities.

entries.clue: Fine beer served up for African resident (5)

entries.clue: Vigorous appetite, yen (5)

entries.clue: Reportedly ready for American anguish (6)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not prepared but British slang for money (as in 'the readies'), so the American's ready is the dollar.
annotation.definitionFit: Dolour is a literary word for grief or anguish.

entries.clue: Organic bananas repelling Mr Munro? (5,4)

annotation.surface: Organic fruit keeps a man called Munro at bay.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Mr Munro' looks like a man's name; 'Mr' is wordplay and a Munro is a Scottish mountain over 3,000 feet. The question mark flags a definition by example.
annotation.definitionFit: Cairn Gorm, in the Scottish Highlands, is one of the Munros.

entries.clue: Starts to look enquiringly at Keir Starmer's dodgy briefings (5)

indicators.note: take the first letter of each of the following words

annotation.walkthrough: Keir Starmer is the British Labour Prime Minister; only his initials matter here.
annotation.definitionFit: A leak is information passed unofficially to the press, a dodgy kind of briefing.

entries.clue: Answer negative from Macron immediately (4)

blocks.note: 'non' is French for no; Emmanuel Macron is the French president

annotation.surface: The French president gives a flat no without hesitation.
annotation.walkthrough: Macron stands for France, so his negative is NON. Anon now usually means 'soon', but its older sense is 'at once'.

entries.clue: Turbulence until embraced by very old non-clerics (10)

til is a short form of until, placed inside LAITY: LA-TIL-ITY

annotation.surface: Upheaval lasts until the elderly congregation takes things in hand.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Non-clerics' is a roundabout way to say the laity, ordinary church members as opposed to clergy; 'til' is the informal short form of until.

entries.clue: Boy unsheathed sword (3)

blocks.note: BLADE loses its outer letters B and E

annotation.surface: A boy draws a sword from its scabbard.
annotation.walkthrough: The sword is a BLADE, and stripping its outside leaves LAD.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lad is an informal word for a boy or young man.

entries.clue: Papers eviscerated leftie disliking work (4)

indicators.note: to eviscerate is to remove the insides, leaving only the outer letters

annotation.surface: Newspapers savage a work-shy left-winger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Papers' suggests the press; it is identity papers, ID.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone idle is lazy and averse to work.

entries.clue: Privileged individual jailed, back in Dartmoor (7)

indicators.note: the back of Dartmoor is its last letter

annotation.surface: A well-connected person ends up behind bars back at Dartmoor.
annotation.walkthrough: Dartmoor is a well-known English prison, which makes 'back in Dartmoor' read as a return to jail.
annotation.definitionFit: An insider is someone with privileged access to an organisation.

entries.clue: Retired in Toulouse, D'Artagnan deals in financial products (6)

the answer lies inside the words that follow

annotation.surface: D'Artagnan, the musketeer, retires to Toulouse and plays the markets.
annotation.walkthrough: The run SEDART spans the break between the two names; read backwards it gives the answer.
annotation.definitionFit: To trade is to buy and sell, here in financial products such as stocks.

entries.clue: Swear nothing concealed by Head of Audi (German car firm) (4)

indicators.note: the O is hidden inside VW
take the first letter of Audi

annotation.walkthrough: The bracket reads as an explanation of Audi; it is its own piece of wordplay, VW, which Audi's owner happens to be.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to avow is to state openly and solemnly, as one does under oath.

entries.clue: Remember wee Kenny securing a fast time? (5-4)

indicators.note: the outer words hold the answer fast inside them

entries.clue: Strong and solid ending for Babes in the Wood (8)

last letter of BabeS, placed inside THICKET

entries.clue: My clue shocked college (6)

entries.clue: Vehicle air-conditioning turned on, heading for Rye (3)

entries.clue: In Germany with little sister, occupied by ordinary division of cells (7)

entries.clue: Bear periodically brash pompous official (4-3)

entries.clue: A few drinks and a sandwich (5)
